subject: Peak season price-hold extension request
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@retailgen.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@retailgen.com>, RetailGen Procurement <procurement@retailgen.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short price-hold extension for Q4 peak season

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you had a good weekend — quick ask from our side. We are entering our Q4 promotional run earlier this year and expect token consumption to spike ~2.5x across November. We are under contract to renew in December, but procurement is pushing for visibility on pricing during the peak window.

Can Redwood extend the current price-hold (our rate card) through 2026-12-31 if we agree to a temporary, one-quarter commit increase (estimated +35% of current monthly commit for Oct–Dec)? Procurement wants an explicit price guard for the promotional period before they sign the annual amendment.

Attached is a short note from our finance team with consumption projections. Can you let me know if this is feasible and the minimal commercial terms you would need?

Thanks — Elena

--
Elena Morris
Head of Data Products, RetailGen
elena@retailgen.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@retailgen.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@retailgen.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short price-hold extension for Q4 peak season

Hi Elena — appreciate the heads up and the attachment. Short answer: yes, we can structure a conditional price-hold through 2026-12-31. High-level options that would work from our side: 

1) Temporary Commit Increase (Preferred)
   - RetailGen increases monthly committed units by 35% for Oct–Dec (three months).
   - We hold current rates (no usage-based uplift) for peak usage up to 125% of the increased commit monthly. Overage beyond that billed at standard overage rates.
   - One-time implementation credit of 5% on the next invoice to offset migration/engineering costs.

2) Short-term Retainer + Price Hold
   - Maintain current commit, add a fixed retainer fee for Oct–Dec that buys a capped rate-hold up to projected peak. Retainer refundable against overage. 

3) Alternate: Volume-tier step-up with a 60-day notice where price-hold is phased out to a blended rate.

If you go with option 1 we can produce an amendment (simple 1-page schedule) and fast-track legal review. Practically we need: expected monthly token target for Oct/Nov/Dec (so ops can size burst capacity), and procurement sign-off on the commit increase. Rishi — can you confirm SLA impact and capacity?

I can loop in Monica from CS to help with onboarding and burst-runbook.

Best,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Request: short price-hold extension for Q4 peak season

Kim / Monica — quick ops note: we can support a temporary +35% commit for Oct–Dec with existing pools if Customer provides a rolling daily forecast and a 24-hour burst window request process. No change to SLA; we'll flag risk if tail latency increases during promotional spikes. Need to reserve additional burst capacity by 2026-09-21 to avoid cold-start delays.

Marissa — commercial implications: the 5% implementation credit is acceptable; recommend we tie the price-hold to the commit increase with a written clause that the hold expires 2026-12-31 unless an annual amendment is executed before renewal. Also propose a small early-exit fee if RetailGen reduces base commit within 90 days post-promotions to prevent churn gaming.

Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morris <elena@retailgen.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@retailgen.com>, RetailGen Procurement <procurement@retailgen.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short price-hold extension for Q4 peak season

Thanks Kim — that sounds promising. Procurement is okay with a temporary commit increase but they want: (a) an explicit price-hold clause through 2026-12-31, (b) a clause stating the hold only applies while the increased commit is active, and (c) a short transition plan if we move to an annual amendment (no retroactive price changes during the promotional period).

Two asks from our side: could you remove the early-exit fee if the variance is <=10% across the following quarter (we are committing +/- forecasting noise), and can you confirm the implementation credit can be applied within the first billing cycle after Oct 1? Procurement also wants to see a one-page amendment draft for legal.

If you can send a draft amendment, I can route to our legal and procurement for sign-off.

Best,
Elena
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@retailgen.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short price-hold extension for Q4 peak season — draft attached

Elena — attaching a short amendment draft (also shared to the Drive link). Key points we adjusted per your asks:

- Price-hold effective 2026-10-01 through 2026-12-31 when RetailGen increases monthly committed units by 35%.
- Hold applies only to usage within the capped threshold (125% of the increased commit).
- Implementation credit (5%) applied to first invoice after Oct 1.
- Removed early-exit fee for <=10% variance in following quarter.
- Transition language: if both parties execute the annual amendment before 2026-12-31, the promotional usage will be billed per the executed annual rates (no retroactive increases).

Next steps: if this looks good I will ping Legal to open a slim DocuSign packet and we’ll schedule a 15-min procurement handoff with Tom if needed. Monica will follow up on the burst-runbook and the daily forecast template.

Thanks — looking forward to getting RetailGen through the season.

Best,
Kim
